task_specification.objective: Advance release convergence by repairing both active player-facing defects, restoring an authored cemetery spatial contract that is traversable and visually stable, and making dense profiling recapture-ready without claiming software-renderer qualification.

diagnosis.root_cause: Release convergence is split across three independent product families: physical input ownership, upgrade-draft eligibility/presentation, and authored-world/performance qualification. The frozen review still records the Start routing defect and single-actionable-card defect, while spatial and dense results remain unqualified.

stop_conditions: Exactly three bounded tasks are executed in order: HUD/input, ordinary spatial/release, then dense performance.

The union of task.gap_ids is exactly gap:release_convergence_camera_movement_dash_contract, gap:release_convergence_experience_upgrade_transaction_contract, and gap:release_convergence_dense_run_performance_contract, with each appearing once.
Active issue ids finding.gamepad_start_pause_unbound and finding.upgrade_draft_only_one_enabled each appear exactly once; deferred issue ids are not assigned.
Tester owns runtime recapture, visual review, issue closure, and phase verdict; Developer owns only candidate repairs and candidate-owned instrumentation.

strategy.rationale: Use materially different root-cause treatments: explicit physical pause ownership plus direct three-card eligibility/application repair; direct authored-instance/AABB rebinding with an isolated outer datum for spatial integrity instead of another camera-only transform tweak; and hardware-gated dense budgeting/receipt hardening that preserves software evidence as rejected while enabling native three-cycle recapture.

code: Run bounded static/Godot checks on touched candidate files: parse project.godot input actions, verify no duplicate Start/context_back ownership, validate the upgrade catalog and presenter/controller scripts, and assert dense contract constants, release guard, bucket caps, and lifecycle idempotency.
Check mechanically that each required gap appears exactly once and each active issue appears exactly once.
runtime: Tester recaptures active gameplay Start pause/resume and all three upgrade-card focus/confirm paths with authoritative receipts.

Tester runs sparse spatial probes at spawn, central building/landmark, cracked bell near-contact, perimeter/boundary, and ordinary movement/movement replay states, then recaptures ordinary route and terminal lifecycle.

Tester runs the serial native dense protocol at 1920x1080 for three cycles, retaining rejected software evidence when hardware eligibility is false, and owns issue closure and release-convergence verdict.
visual: Inspect the upgrade draft at native, fullscreen, windowed, and supported UI scales for visual hierarchy led by silhouettes or icons, truthful current-to-new values, no more than three decision-relevant stat deltas, stable card dimensions, and distinct keyboard, mouse, and gamepad focus states.

Inspect shipped gameplay frames from spawn, central landmark approaches, perimeter, and dense wave/boss states for larger traversable scale, external depth, landmark visibility, collision alignment, no disappearance/occlusion drift, readable telegraphs, and an unobstructed escape lane.

done_when: Gamepad Start dispatches the pause action during active gameplay, toggles to paused, and toggles back to active on a second press without dispatching context_back or ui_cancel; B/View remains context_back and Escape remains the single keyboard pause owner.

The upgrade draft always exposes three eligible, actionable cards; CardA, CardB, and CardC each accept keyboard, mouse, and gamepad focus and confirm, held confirm is debounced, and exactly one authoritative choice is applied before gameplay resumes.

Each visible card uses a clear visual hierarchy led by silhouettes or icons, shows truthful current-to-new values, and shows no more than three decision-relevant stat deltas; placeholders and unchanged rows are omitted, dimensions remain stable, and focus, hover, pressed, unavailable, and selected states are distinct.
A direct black-box and white-box retest can inspect the pause binding audit, card enabled states, authoritative offered ids, selected id/rank, applied modifier, and exactly-once transaction receipt.
tasks.instructions: Repair the player-facing choice and input ownership surfaces. Rebind the gamepad Start physical event so pause is its sole active-gameplay destination, preserving B/View as context_back and Escape as the single keyboard pause owner; update the router/run-shell handoff only as needed to prevent duplicate dispatch. In the real upgrade-draft controller/presenter, replace any fixture or slot-specific disable path with data-driven eligibility and a deterministic three-card fallback. The shipped choice surface must present a visual hierarchy led by silhouettes or icons, truthful current-to-new values, no more than three decision-relevant stat deltas, restrained copy, and complete keyboard, mouse, and gamepad focus states. Preserve the existing authored iconography and compact hierarchy while making every displayed option selectable and applying the selected modifier exactly once before unpausing.
tasks.title: Repair pause ownership and visual-hierarchy choice transaction

done_when: A fresh ordinary run reaches a stable gameplay state with a larger traversable scale than the current camera-sized pad, while retaining one intact authored cemetery package and a continuous external world/external depth band outside the playable streets.

The camera remains high-angle and arena-readable during ordinary movement and dash; damping does not hide imminent threats, and the central building/landmark set (keeper lantern post, small mausoleum, cracked moon bell) remains visible from spawn and cardinal approaches without disappearance caused by occlusion drift.

Rendered footprints and gameplay collision agree for the cracked bell and other prominent landmarks; traversal cannot pass through them, float above them, or hit an invisible barrier, and the boundary/perimeter remains sealed without trapping the player.

Ordinary movement/movement replay from multiple sides reaches each landmark sight lane and perimeter, with stable visibility and no disappearance/occlusion failure; the authored package remains the sole visual environment and additive outer datum is limited to collision, navigation, spawn/objective anchors.

A direct black-box plus white-box retest can inspect rendered bounds, collision bounds, route anchors, spawn clearance, perimeter state, camera visibility, dash state, and ordinary-route safety receipts.
tasks.instructions: Restore the authored cemetery world as the spatial owner using a materially different direct-instance/AABB rebinding strategy. Inspect the intact AuthoredCemeteryPackage and derive the outer datum, route anchors, and landmark collision from its rendered world-space bounds; remove inherited scene overrides or proxy pads that can desynchronize collision from visuals. Keep a larger traversable scale plus continuous external world/external depth, preserve camera-aware sight lanes and the high-angle movement/dash contract, and explicitly validate the central building/landmark, collision, disappearance/occlusion, boundary/perimeter, and ordinary movement/movement replay terms across spawn, cardinal approaches, and near-contact traversal. Keep the Warden motor, automatic combat, dash state machine, and accepted authored assets intact; only adjust directly related world binding, route, camera-coverage, and lifecycle handoff code.
tasks.title: Rebind authored cemetery scale, landmarks, collision, and perimeter

done_when: The dense profile remains editor-only and release-disabled, records nonzero frame and physics samples before renderer gating, and never reports a software-renderer run as qualified.

A native renderer at 1920x1080 with 25–40 active ordinary enemies records three serial prepare→advance→reset cycles, each with bounded frame-time distributions, capped sample/history growth, and zero live actors plus clean input context after reset.

Dense scheduling keeps authoritative combat/death/drop/pool-retirement events exact while amortising non-authoritative neighbor, steering, vitality, presentation, light, and optional-effect work; representative telegraphs and threats remain readable.

Cycle receipts include renderer classification, hardware eligibility, viewport, sample availability, cycle identity, setup/advance generations, lifecycle deltas, reset isolation, and release-guard status; delayed callbacks cannot replace cycle identity or run serial.
A direct white-box check covers the dense contract, work buckets, renderer gate order, and cleanup invariants; Tester then performs native recapture and owns qualification.
tasks.instructions: Harden the candidate-owned dense performance seam for the host's native qualification pass. Keep the existing hardware gate and software-evidence policy, but audit the dense profile and RunController lifecycle for bounded allocations, pooled actor cleanup, capped histories, deterministic bucket scheduling, and idempotent prepare/advance/reset receipts. Ensure the profile's 1920x1080, 25–40-enemy window is a real playable dense encounter when enabled, without changing ordinary release presentation or introducing tester actions into release exports. Do not claim llvmpipe/software qualification; expose precise handoff data so the host can run three native retries after the ordinary product tasks are complete.
tasks.title: Make dense native qualification recapture-ready
